references.text: The same instruction to carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place is repeated in connection with the regulations for the burnt offering.
At the consecration of Aaron and his sons, the bull for the sin offering was burned outside the camp, in accordance with this regulation.
The meat and skin of the sin offering were burned with fire outside the camp, as prescribed here.
On the Day of Atonement, the bull and the goat for the sin offering were to be burned outside the camp, and whoever burned them had to wash before returning.
The red heifer was to be led outside the camp and completely burned, including the ashes which were to be gathered at a clean place.
Hebrews explains that Jesus suffered outside the city gate to sanctify the people with his own blood, fulfilling the burning of the sin offering outside the camp.
